name: Short-Stay Visa / Visa-Free Entry

requirement_groups.name: Visa-free entry for citizens of 38 European countries

requirements.blocker_text: Citizens of 38 named European countries may enter visa-free for up to 30 days per entry (90 days for Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia including Latvian non-citizens), capped at 90 total days per calendar year, via any international road/rail border crossing or airport. This regime is a unilateral, presidentially-extended temporary measure, currently valid through 31 December 2026 -- not a permanent legal status.

requirement_groups.name: Short-stay visa (Type C) for other nationalities

requirements.blocker_text: Nationals not covered by the visa-free regime require a Type C short-stay visa, single/double/multiple-entry, valid for stays up to 90 days.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for a Type C visa at a Belarusian embassy/consulate.

outcome.duration_length: 30 days per entry (90 for Poland/Lithuania/Latvia), capped at 90 days/year under the visa-free regime; up to 90 days under a Type C visa

sources.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Belarus -- Visa-Free Entry for Citizens of a Number of European Countries: 38 countries, 30/90-day allowances, 90-day annual cap, extended through 31 December 2026, no transit to Russia under this regime
Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Belarus -- Entry Visas: Type B (transit), Type C (short-stay, up to 90 days), Type D (long-stay, up to 5 years) categories

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Belarus). Belarus is under significant sanctions and travel-restriction pressure; several EU/Schengen countries maintain their own restrictions on issuing visas to Belarusian citizens or on land-border crossings with Belarus (not modeled here, since this route concerns FOREIGNERS entering Belarus, not Belarusians travelling out). The visa-free regime is explicitly a temporary, unilaterally-extended measure (currently through 31 December 2026) rather than a permanent treaty-based arrangement -- flagged since it could be discontinued, shortened, or further extended at the Belarusian president's discretion, unlike EU Schengen rules which are treaty-bound.
